parsed.explanation: The dossier documents state-directed enforcement against gender presentation itself: a 2021 court sentenced two transgender women to the five-year statutory maximum for wearing women's clothing, on no proof of acts; a 2011 appearance-based conviction followed the same pattern; 2022 saw arbitrary arrests of people for gender nonconformity with detainees beaten by gendarmes. A 2020 assessment ranks this among the world's most aggressive prosecutors of same-sex conduct, and the law is explicitly used as a lever against visibly gender-nonconforming people (tier 2, organised/state targeting) with extortion, public beatings described as common, a raided LGBTQ organisation, few willing lawyers, and a 'hell' prison. Recourse is thin: appeals sometimes succeed (2013 acquittal) but detention is severe and prolonged. No execution is documented, keeping this above the 0.05 tier, but documented state targeting with maximum sentences for presentation places this at the top of the Severe Risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry screening or refusal rule for trans visitors is documented; failure-to-carry-identification was charged in the 2021 case, so document irregularity compounds substantive charges.
entry_documents.interaction: Document checks during police stops can trigger the anti-homosexuality/appearance enforcement chain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans women held five months then sentenced to five years (maximum) for presentation; 2022 arbitrary arrests and detention with gendarme beatings; main prison described as 'hell'; coerced 'proof' exams threatened in 2005.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Appeals sometimes succeed (2013 acquittal; 2021 release pending appeal), but judges convicted without proof of acts.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest on appearance grounds leads into prolonged custody, prosecution, and imprisonment without reliable judicial check.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Custodial placement and prison conditions for trans detainees not detailed; documented beatings and 'hell' conditions in the main prison.

care_services.exposure: Health material is coercive only (threatened forensic examinations); medication and trans care access unresolved; medication confiscation risk unaddressed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 347-1 (up to five years) plus appearance-based sentences of six months to five years; Article 83 cybercrime penalties; police harassment, extortion, false allegations; 2020 assessment: among world's most aggressive prosecutors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: President urged privacy after 2006 tabloid outing; state communication council criticised it; prosecutions nonetheless continued.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law licenses both civilians and security forces to abuse with impunity, per HRW-source statement.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific policy documented; a minor accompanying a trans adult shares exposure to appearance-based arrest and the adult's detention/separation.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult's arrest would separate the child; no documented safeguarding mechanism.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Public beatings of gay and trans people described as common; 2022 group attacks on victims followed by security-force arrest of the victims; police extortion documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; police are themselves perpetrators or abettors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims calling police risk arrest and beating, not protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Few lawyers willing to take these cases; LGBTQ organisation shut down by police raid; 2021 appeal unresolved; enforcement documented through March 2022 with none later in the record.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Appellate acquittals show courts occasionally correct the worst outcomes, but slowly and unpredictably.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Weak recourse raises severity of every documented exposure; last documented incident 2022, current practice unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very similar: morality-based arrests on presentation grounds, maximum-term sentences without proof of acts, beaten detainees, no credible recourse. Lacks 0.15-C's decoy sweeps and capital clause ambiguity, so slightly above.

Comparable severity: multi-month pretrial custody, maximum sentences for presentation, stereotyped evidentiary standards, illusory appeals. No unaffordable-bail/compelled-confession machine documented, so marginally less bad.

More severe than 0.25-D: here convictions reach the five-year maximum for mere clothing, beatings are common, and the state prosecutes aggressively by international assessment; 0.25-D's annulled-appeals pattern is weaker recourse than documented here.
Below 0.05-B: no execution documented for these offences and no death in custody; appellate acquittal occurred, which the 0.05 tier lacks entirely.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a single national criminal-law system enforced against gender presentation: Article 347-1 plus appearance-based charging produced a five-year maximum sentence for two trans women in a restaurant, and 2022 security-force arrests of gender-nonconforming people with beatings show the pattern is current and state-directed. This is tier-2 organised state targeting with a documented tier-3/4 consequences ladder (arrest, months of custody, maximum imprisonment, prison abuse, extortion, public beatings). The visitor cannot avoid the exposure: presentation alone has twice sufficed for conviction. Mitigation is weak and intermittent — occasional appellate acquittals, a presidential privacy statement that changed nothing. No execution documented, and the most recent recorded enforcement is 2022, but nothing suggests the regime has softened. Severe Risk, near the band's upper edge.
